Calendar months and seasons as date windows

Source: R/wet_windows_calendar.R
wet_windows_calendar.Rd

The twelve months and four meteorological seasons in the windows format wet_window_stats() takes: a name and month-day start and end, both inclusive. An end of "02-29" means the last day of February in leap and common years alike.

Usage

wet_windows_calendar()

Value

data.frame(window, start, end) with 16 rows.

Details

The seasons are named djf, mam, jja and son rather than winter, spring and so on. That is deliberate: cd::cd_seasons() builds winter from December, January and February of one calendar year, while here djf is the contiguous December to February and takes the year of its December, so the two would disagree under the same name.

Examples

wet_windows_calendar()
#>    window start   end
#> 1     jan 01-01 01-31
#> 2     feb 02-01 02-29
#> 3     mar 03-01 03-31
#> 4     apr 04-01 04-30
#> 5     may 05-01 05-31
#> 6     jun 06-01 06-30
#> 7     jul 07-01 07-31
#> 8     aug 08-01 08-31
#> 9     sep 09-01 09-30
#> 10    oct 10-01 10-31
#> 11    nov 11-01 11-30
#> 12    dec 12-01 12-31
#> 13    djf 12-01 02-29
#> 14    mam 03-01 05-31
#> 15    jja 06-01 08-31
#> 16    son 09-01 11-30

# Add a species window to the calendar ones
rbind(wet_windows_calendar(),
      data.frame(window = "ch_spawning", start = "08-01", end = "09-15"))
#>         window start   end
#> 1          jan 01-01 01-31
#> 2          feb 02-01 02-29
#> 3          mar 03-01 03-31
#> 4          apr 04-01 04-30
#> 5          may 05-01 05-31
#> 6          jun 06-01 06-30
#> 7          jul 07-01 07-31
#> 8          aug 08-01 08-31
#> 9          sep 09-01 09-30
#> 10         oct 10-01 10-31
#> 11         nov 11-01 11-30
#> 12         dec 12-01 12-31
#> 13         djf 12-01 02-29
#> 14         mam 03-01 05-31
#> 15         jja 06-01 08-31
#> 16         son 09-01 11-30
#> 17 ch_spawning 08-01 09-15
